articles.title: US unveils proposed tariffs on major partners, including EU and China
articles.description: The United States on Wednesday unveiled proposed tariffs on 14 economies including the European Union and China, after a months-long probe into alleged excess production – the latest move by US President Donald Trump to remake Washington's trade relationships. The new tariffs will need to undergo a period of public comment before taking effect. The new levies target some of the United States' largest trading partners. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

related.title: Trump announces new tariffs on EU, China despite US midterms defeat
related.description: President Donald Trump's administration on Wednesday reignited global trade tensions by proposing new tariffs on some of the largest US trading partners, including the EU, Japan and Taiwan. China could be slapped with a 20 percent tariff, a senior official said. The announcement came weeks after a cost-of-living crisis landed the Republicans a sweeping defeat in the US midterms.

articles.title: Russian casualties in Ukraine war: New reports suggest death toll as high as 700,000
articles.description: New analysis of leaked Russian government data suggests some 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in the war against Ukraine. Independent Russian media outlets have updated their estimates of Moscow's military casualties after Belarusian and Ukrainian hackers obtained figures from the Russian statistics agency.

related.title: Kremlin declines comment on reports 700,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine war
related.description: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Wednesday declined to comment on reports in Russian and international news outlets that around 700,000 Russian soldiers have been killed in the Ukraine war so far. The reports were based on hacked data from Russia's official statistics agency. Peskov said only the defence ministry can disclose figures and told reporters "not to pay attention to any other data".

articles.title: 'We need to stop the war in Iran': US Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal

articles.description: Ukraine will need €115 billion in external financing next year to sustain its economy and war effort against Russia, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, adding that Kyiv had secured commitments for about €90 billion from the European Union.

articles.title: Houthi rebels close in on Aden, Yemeni forces dig in behind fortified line
articles.description: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have advanced to within about 60 kilometers of the seat of Yemen’s internationally recognized government in the southern city of Aden, but the forces fighting them have set up a fortified line to defend the city, a military official said Tuesday. The Houthis' advance toward Aden has come after forces allied with the government withdrew from areas on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, allowing the Houthis to consolidate their grip on territory around the crucial waterway.

articles.title: Colombian authorities rescue all hostages held at Cartagena supermarket
articles.description: Security forces rescued all the hostages held for nearly a day at a supermarket in the northern Colombian tourist city of Cartagena, President Abelardo de la Espriella said early Wednesday. The hostage situation broke out as Colombia is experiencing a wave of attacks by rebel groups on government targets.
